title: A reproducible data investigation
goals: Report results with coverage and uncertainty

prerequisite.prompt: What should happen to an invalid duration instead of silently making it zero?
prerequisite.answer: Record the rejection and reason; preserve the raw value for authorized review.

vocabulary: A documented process for answering a question with evidence
An ordered sequence of processing steps
A record of inputs, decisions and changes
A reason a conclusion has restricted scope

blocks.text: Investigate the fictional question: among supplied sessions with valid duration records, what is the mean duration? Inputs are 10, 0, 20, None and -2 minutes. Our schema accepts exact integers 0 through 60. The wording deliberately limits the answer to accepted records.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The result is 3 accepted, 2 rejected, and mean 10.0 minutes. A reproducible report states the question, raw input version, schema, exclusion reasons, calculation and scope. Someone else should obtain the same result from the same inputs and rules.

blocks.label: If another valid value 30 is added, calculate the new accepted count and mean.

blocks.text: Dividing the accepted total 30 by all five records gives 6 and answers no clear observed-duration question. Use the accepted count for this mean, disclose exclusions, and never describe it as the average for every supplied session.

Missing or invalid durations might belong to unusually long sessions. The accepted mean may therefore differ from the full group's mean. Do not make a causal claim from this descriptive investigation.

blocks.label: A report gives only mean 9. What additional evidence lets a peer reproduce it?

workbook.title: State the question
workbook.prompt: Write the worked investigation question so its population of records is clear.
workbook.answer: What is the mean duration among supplied sessions with valid integer minutes from 0 through 60?

workbook.title: Trace exclusions
workbook.prompt: Classify 0, None, -2 and 60 under the schema.
workbook.answer: 0 and 60 accepted; None missing/unknown and -2 out of range are rejected.

workbook.title: Repair a denominator
workbook.prompt: A report divides a valid total of 24 by six supplied rows, though only three are valid. Correct the valid-record mean.
workbook.answer: 24/3 = 8. Report 3 accepted and 3 rejected; do not use all six as the valid-record denominator.

workbook.title: Investigate independently
workbook.prompt: Analyze raw durations [6, 12, None, 0, 70, 18] with the same schema. Report question, accepted list, rejections, mean and one limitation.
workbook.answer: Accepted [6, 12, 0, 18], 2 rejected, total 36, mean 9. State 4 of 6 accepted; missing/invalid records may differ. Preserve the raw list and rules.

workbook.title: Support reproduction
workbook.prompt: A report gives only mean 9. What additional evidence lets a peer reproduce it?
workbook.answer: Input records/version, schema, excluded rows and reasons, accepted count, calculation and code/configuration version.

teacher.background: Teach Week 30 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. Investigate the fictional question: among supplied sessions with valid duration records, what is the mean duration? Inputs are 10, 0, 20, None and -2 minutes. Our schema accepts exact integers 0 through 60. The wording deliberately limits the answer to accepted records. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.
materials: Python 3 editor with a fresh local practice file
Paper trace table and the student workbook
Fictional input records from this lesson; no real student identifiers
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and explain the purpose in the opening section.
Read the worked example and diagram; ask learners to trace each step aloud.
Complete W1 and W2, then compare predictions with observed results.
Collect the guided prediction before running; discuss a mismatch and its cause.
Retrieve the main rule without showing the previous answer.
Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Four accepted values total 60, so mean 15 minutes; still two rejected. Exit: Input records/version, schema, excluded rows and reasons, accepted count, calculation and code/configuration version.
misconceptions: A successful run proves the conclusion

Missing or invalid durations might belong to unusually long sessions. The accepted mean may therefore differ from the full group's mean. Do not make a causal claim from this descriptive investigation.
Require the new W4 case, explicit predictions and an explanation. Fresh retry: [5, None, 15, -1, 10] gives accepted [5,15,10], 2 rejected and mean 10, with coverage 3 of 5.

Dividing the accepted total 30 by all five records gives 6 and answers no clear observed-duration question. Use the accepted count for this mean, disclose exclusions, and never describe it as the average for every supplied session.
teacher.assessment: Independent W4 evidence: Accepted [6, 12, 0, 18], 2 rejected, total 36, mean 9. State 4 of 6 accepted; missing/invalid records may differ. Preserve the raw list and rules. Record whether the learner needed no help, a hint or explanation. Fresh retry: [5, None, 15, -1, 10] gives accepted [5,15,10], 2 rejected and mean 10, with coverage 3 of 5.
teacher.support: Provide an investigation checklist with blank evidence fields. Extension: compare median and mean of accepted values and explain what each hides.
